title: Acropora DNA Extraction Using Qiagen DNeasy Tissue Kit
author: Iliana Baums
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgjqjumw
materials: Follow Qiagen’s protocol with the following changes: Following step 6 of the spin-column protocol, we perform the optional centrifugation for 1 min at 20,000 xg to dry the column membrane.

steps.title: Cut coral polyps
steps.instruction: Use sterile technique to cut 3–4 polyps (skeleton with tissue) off the coral fragment with a razor blade.

steps.title: Transfer polyps to tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the pieces into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube or a well of a 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Add lysis reagents
steps.instruction: Add 180 µL Buffer ATL and 20 µL proteinase K (Qiagen DNeasy kit) to each tube or well.

steps.title: Mix gently
steps.instruction: If using tubes, invert several times to gently mix the reagents; do not vortex.

steps.title: Lysis incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture overnight at 56 °C; the lysate may acquire a slight yellow hue from algal symbionts.

substeps.instruction: Place tubes or plate on a rocking platform for gentle agitation (optional)

steps.title: First elution (low TE)
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL low‑TE buffer directly to the column membrane, incubate 1 min, then centrifuge as recommended; this eluate contains smaller fragmented DNA.

steps.title: Second elution (high MW)
steps.instruction: Move the column to a new 1.5 mL tube, add 100 µL low‑TE buffer, incubate 5 min, centrifuge as recommended; this eluate contains high‑molecular‑weight DNA and should be stored at –20 °C.

steps.title: Gel electrophoresis check
steps.instruction: Run DNA from both elutions on a 1.5 % agarose gel; look for a high‑molecular‑weight band at the top of the gel with little smearing.
